newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal banks benefitting from portfolio gains.
newsitem.headline: Portugal banks benefitting from portfolio gains.

text.p: Analysts say that they are reviewing profit forecasts for Portuguese banks because big gains on bond portfolios, spurred by the sharp fall in interest rates, look set to swell overall profits in 1996.
"The performance of fixed-rate debt is leading us to revise upwards the (expected) results of the banks in 1996," said Finantia analyst Joao Capucho.
But the impact on share prices was likely to be blunted by the fact that many banking groups are going through expensive restructuring due to recent acquisitions, analysts cautioned.
Banco Portugues de Investimento, for example, is raising capital to help fund its purchase of Banco de Fomento & Exterior.
Analysts see only Banco Comercial Portugues and Banco Espirito Santo outperforming the bourse index during the rest of the year.
"By the end of the year, the overall market could gain another five or six percent. BCP and BES could beat that, but the others no," said analyst Pedro Assumpcao of Central de Investimentos.
In first half 1996, portfolio gains for the five Portuguese banks BFE, BPI, Banco Pinto & Sotto Maior, BCP and BES, totalled some 47.5 billion escudos against 61.0 billion in the whole of 1995.
After a first half in which interest rates fell sharply -- six-month Treasury bills shed 150 basis points -- few analysts anticipated further sharp easing in the last six months of the year.
But growing confidence that Portugal and Spain can qualify for the European Union's planned Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) has driven bond and money market yields to record lows.
"Trading profits (of the five banks) should be pretty good in this half as well," said Assumpcao. "I believe they could reach 80-90 billion escudos," he said.
Capucho saw portfolio gains at between 75 and 80 billion.
"The third quarter (results) should see some of these profits in the accounts but they are likely to be much more explicit in the fourth quarter," said another analyst.
The majority of analysts contacted by Reuters saw the share prices of BCP and BES benefiting most.
BCP is about to finish the restructuring that followed the takeover of Banco Portugues do Atlantico, while BES has preferred the organic route to growth to acquiring assets.
BCP stock has the most upside potential after underperforming heavily in the past months due to the bank's capital call earlier in the year, analysts said.
"I bet more in BCP because its (shares) fell violently with the capital call. I don't think the (current) level is normal for BCP," said Assumpcao.
Since the beginning of the year, BCP shares have lost 3.1 percent while the PSI20 index of leading shares has gained more than 20 percent. BES advanced 16.3 percent in the period.
